title: Project store with encrypted staging credentials

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 STATIC AUDIT — SPRINT 2 — ROUND 1 — VERDICT: CONDITIONAL (one required fix, everything else is clean)
Audited commit 0eff6eef2c19f41d23dba9b075097529e8f44acc against base 11bca26 (Sprint 1 close). Working tree clean; committed code.
Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. No cross-version ("arrives between release A and B") criterion in this sprint. Requirement 11's factual premise (bfcache handler lived in views/landing.ejs only at base) confirmed by grep against 11bca26.
Handoff text arrived partially garbled in transit; audited against the sprint file and the code, not the handoff.

=== THE BLOCKER ===
[HIGH — requirement 7 violated for the ranges it names] IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals bypass the private-address rejection. src/lib/ipRangeCheck.js:38.
isPrivateIPv6 matches /^::ffff:(\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)$/ — the DOTTED mapped form. But the WHATWG URL parser (new URL(), urlValidation.js:72) serializes every IPv6 host to compressed HEX form before the check ever sees it. new URL('http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/').hostname is '[::ffff:7f00:1]', not '[::ffff:127.0.0.1]'. The regex never matches on the real code path.
DEMONSTRATED three ways:
  1. normalizeAndValidateUrl() ACCEPTS all of: http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/, http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/ (both = 127.0.0.1), http://[::ffff:c0a8:10a]/ (= 192.168.1.10, the acceptance-criteria example address), http://[::ffff:a00:1]/ (= 10.0.0.1). Each is stored as a valid URL.
  2. isPrivateOrReservedAddress('::ffff:7f00:1') -> false; isPrivateOrReservedAddress('::ffff:127.0.0.1') -> true. The function is correct for a string it never receives.
  3. Reachability: started an HTTP server bound ONLY to 127.0.0.1, then fetch()'d the URL the validator accepted (http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:PORT/). Response: 200 "LOOPBACK-REACHED". The accepted URL reaches IPv4 loopback on this machine.
Why the suite didn't catch it: test/lib/ipRangeCheck.test.js:19-20 feeds the dotted strings straight to isPrivateOrReservedAddress, bypassing new URL(). test/lib/urlValidation.test.js has no IPv4-mapped case at all. The unit test proves the function works on input it never gets; the integration path is untested for this shape. This is exactly the check Dev Team's handoff called out as "added beyond requirement 7's literal list" — the claim was made, and the claim is false on the only path that matters.
Why it's a gate failure and not a note: requirement 7 names 127.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16. ::ffff:<addr> IS that address on any dual-stack host; the sprint calls this the SSRF surface's "first line of defence" and the Risks section says both layers are required. A filter with a known, trivial, documented bypass for the exact ranges it names is not a first line of defence.
FIX (Dev Team's call how, this is the shape): either (a) replace the regex with a real parser — expand the IPv6 address, detect the ::ffff:0:0/96 prefix, convert the low 32 bits to dotted IPv4 and run isPrivateIPv4 on that; or (b) use node's net.BlockList, which handles IPv4-mapped addresses natively (addSubnet the six ranges as ipv4 plus ::1, then check(addr, family)). Add a urlValidation-level test that goes through new URL() with a bracketed mapped literal in BOTH dotted and hex spellings, so the test exercises the real path. Authoring that test is Dev Team's job, not mine.

=== REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE — 10 of 11 met; req 7 partially met ===
1. Persistent single-file store, required schema — MET. node:sqlite (built-in, zero new deps), src/db/database.js. All eight columns present. data/ gitignored, never tracked.
2. AES-256-GCM, ENCRYPTION_KEY hard-fail — MET, verified directly. src/lib/crypto.js: aes-256-gcm, 12-byte random IV from crypto.randomBytes on every call, no code path accepts a caller-supplied IV, auth tag verified on decrypt. Startup asserted on printed text for all four failure shapes: unset and empty both print "Missing required environment variable: ENCRYPTION_KEY. Set it in your .env file..."; 32-hex (16 bytes) and 64-non-hex both print "Invalid environment variable: ENCRYPTION_KEY must be a 64-character hex string (32 bytes) for AES-256-GCM..." No default or fallback expression for the key anywhere in src/.
3. Decrypt for outbound use only; never rendered/logged/JSON'd — MET, verified. getDecryptedBasicAuthPassword is defined in projectsRepository.js and called from nowhere in src/ or views/. rowToProject omits the encrypted column entirely (a boolean hasPassword survives, nothing else). No console.log/res.json in src/ can carry a password. Rendered edit + list HTML greped for the plaintext sentinel and for the ciphertext shape: neither present. Password <input> renders with no value attribute.
4. Full CRUD behind auth, url() helper — MET. List/new/create/edit/update/delete-confirm/delete in src/routes/projects.js, mounted after requireAuth. Unauthenticated GET /projects -> 302 login (tested). Every internal href/action goes through url(); the only raw hrefs are the user's own validated external live/staging URLs (correct — those are not internal). All verified at BASE_PATH=/content-check.
5. Edit-form password rule (blank keeps / value replaces / clear removes) — MET, verified by test and by live HTTP. Repository test walks all three transitions in sequence with decrypt assertions at each step; integration test does the same over HTTP. Edit screen renders "A password is currently stored. Leave blank to keep it..." with an empty password field and the clear control present. Validation-error re-render does NOT echo a typed password back into the HTML (checked with a sentinel).
6. URL validation + normalization — MET, verified. All four acceptance-criteria cases asserted on the field-level message via the real form: ftp:// and bare domain -> "Enter a full URL starting with http:// or https://."; empty -> "This field is required."; http://192.168.1.10/ -> "This URL points to a private, loopback, or link-local address, which this tool cannot fetch." Trailing slash stripped from a bare origin only; real paths preserved (correct reading of "from the origin").
7. Private-range rejection — PARTIALLY MET. Literal dotted IPv4 in every listed range: rejected. Alternate IPv4 spellings (hex 0x7f000001, decimal 2130706433, short 127.1, octal 0177.0.0.1): all rejected, because WHATWG normalizes them to dotted before the check — good. ::1: rejected. localhost via /etc/hosts: rejected. IPv4-MAPPED IPv6 LITERALS: ACCEPTED — see THE BLOCKER.
8. Delete removes credentials entirely — MET at the logical store level, verified at the raw SQL layer (SELECT after DELETE returns nothing; no soft-delete, no tombstone). See ISSUE 2 for a file-level note.
9. Unit tests for the four named areas — MET. crypto round-trip + unique-IV + wrong-key + tamper; blank-keeps rule in sequence; URL accept/reject; private-range with boundary cases on both sides of 172.16/12 and 192.168/16. 110 tests pass, lint exit 0, tests never touch disk (verified: no data/ dir created by the run).
10. CSRF on every state-changing route — MET, verified live. Create/edit/delete POSTs without a token -> 403 rendering error.ejs as text/html with "This form's session token was missing or expired..."; bad token -> 403; valid token -> 302. Delete with no token leaves the row intact. Token is 32 random bytes per session, compared length-checked then timingSafeEqual (the length pre-check matters — timingSafeEqual throws on mismatch, and the test covers it).
11. Cache-Control: no-store + shared bfcache guard — MET, verified. GET /projects and GET /projects/:id/edit both return "no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate" (asserted on the header). bfcache pageshow/persisted handler moved out of landing.ejs into views/partials/bfcache-guard.ejs, included via partials/head.ejs by every authenticated view (landing, error, list, form, delete-confirm — grep-confirmed, one include each). login.ejs correctly excluded. This is exactly what the sprint asked for: a shared layout so the next screen can't forget it.

=== CODE QUALITY ===
Test coverage: Strong. Unit + repository + middleware + HTTP integration. Negative assertions throughout. The one hole is the blocker above — a unit test that proves a function on input the real path never produces.
Error handling: Good. Every route wraps in try/next(err). decrypt throws on tamper and nothing swallows it. DNS lookup failure is the one deliberate catch-and-continue, documented in place with the reasoning (see Q&A).
Standards: Follows the Sprint 1 shape — DI factories, prepared statements once, one module owns the encrypted column. Repository is injectable so tests use :memory:. No shared types redefined. Sprint 1 audit issues 1 (cookie-name constant) and 3 (cookie path scoped to BASE_PATH) are confirmed fixed in the interim fix loop.
Security: Everything except the blocker is right. GCM with per-call random nonce, key validated for byte length not string length, no plaintext at rest (raw file scanned for the sentinel: absent), CSRF constant-time, EJS escaping on all user-supplied strings, external hrefs limited to http/https by validation so no javascript: scheme can land in an anchor.

=== OTHER ISSUES — none block; fold into the fix commit or a later sprint ===
2. [LOW] Deleted ciphertext persists in freed SQLite pages. src/db/projectsRepository.js:132. DEMONSTRATED: after DELETE (no VACUUM), the encrypted blob is still findable in the raw file bytes; after VACUUM it is not. This is ciphertext, so it's within the sprint's stated threat model ("a leaked database file alone does not hand over client infrastructure") and requirement 8 is about the logical store, which is clean. But "leaves no trace" is cheap to make literally true: PRAGMA secure_delete = ON in openDatabase() zeroes freed content on delete. One line.
3. [LOW] Addresses outside requirement 7's list are accepted: 0.0.0.0, [::], [fe80::]/10 (IPv6 link-local), [fc00::]/7 (IPv6 unique-local). DEMONSTRATED: all four accepted by the validator. Not a requirement violation — the list is explicit — but 0.0.0.0 reaching localhost is a well-known SSRF trick and IPv6 link-local is the IPv6 twin of 169.254/16 which IS listed. If Dev Team goes the net.BlockList route for the blocker, adding these is a few more addSubnet lines. Master Controller should decide whether to widen the list in Sprint 3's request-time check.
4. [LOW] values.rawPassword is passed into the template scope on validation-error re-render (routes/projects.js:53, :89 via the spread of values). It is NOT rendered — verified with a sentinel — but a plaintext password sitting in EJS locals is a footgun for whoever adds a debug dump or a hidden field later. Strip rawPassword from values before render.
5. [INFO] URL normalization via parsed.origin silently drops userinfo: "https://user:pw@staging.example.com/" saves as "https://staging.example.com". Probably desirable (credentials belong in the dedicated fields) but nobody told the user. Consider a field-level message or a note in the form hint.

=== ANSWERS TO DEV TEAM'S QUESTIONS ===
Q: "Clear credentials" clears the username too — does that match PRD intent?
A: Yes. A basic-auth credential is a pair; a stored username with no password is not a credential, it's a stale hint. Requirement 5's "removes it" reads naturally as "removes the credential." The control is labelled "Clear stored credentials" (plural) so the UI says what it does. Keep it. If someone wants to keep the username and drop only the password, they can retype the username on the next edit — that's the rare path, not the common one.
Q: DNS failure allows through — right call, or fail closed?
A: Allow-through is acceptable here, with two conditions, and I want both on the record. (1) It is only acceptable because the sprint's Risks section makes Sprint 3's request-time check a hard requirement, not defence-in-depth-if-convenient. An unresolvable name can't be fetched today, and a name that later resolves to something private must be caught at fetch time regardless of what save-time did — DNS rebinding makes that true even for names that resolve fine now. (2) The workflow argument is real: PRD §4.2 says credentials must be EASILY updated, staging hosts go dark between rebuilds, and a save-time hard fail on an unresolvable staging URL would block exactly the "update the login for the site that's being rebuilt right now" edit the PRD cares most about. So: keep it, keep the comment explaining why, and QA1 will be checking Sprint 3 for the request-time check that this decision depends on. One correction to the handoff: the sprint file does not actually contain "a risk note on staging domains going dark" — the Context section says staging sites are rebuilt constantly, which supports the same conclusion, but cite what's there.

=== FOR THE RE-AUDIT ===
The blocker is isolated to src/lib/ipRangeCheck.js (and the tests that should cover it). If the fix commit touches only that plus tests, the re-audit will be fast: I'll re-run the mapped-literal probes through new URL() in both spellings and re-run the loopback reachability check, and re-verify the tree. I will not re-derive the other ten requirements unless the diff reaches them.

PASS: QA1 STATIC AUDIT — SPRINT 2 — ROUND 2 (RE-AUDIT) — VERDICT: PASS
Audited commit dd4be40d470f290d6105b2c04ac7e27c571a3481. Working tree clean; committed code.
Sprint file: byte-identical to the copy read fresh at round 1 of this session (git diff 0eff6ee..dd4be40 on docs/sprints/2-in-progress/ is empty; sha256 e7e40c50...). No cross-version criterion applies. Requirements unchanged, so this round is focused on what moved; the round-1 findings on the other ten requirements stand as recorded.

SCOPE OF THE FIX — as narrow as claimed, verified by git diff --stat 0eff6ee dd4be40:
  src/lib/ipRangeCheck.js (rewritten), test/lib/ipRangeCheck.test.js (+3 hex-spelling cases), test/lib/urlValidation.test.js (+4 end-to-end bracketed cases), docs/sprints/state/sprint-2.json (lifecycle bookkeeping). Nothing else touched.

THE ROUND-1 BLOCKER — RESOLVED, DEMONSTRATED
Fix: hand-rolled octet/regex comparison replaced with node:net BlockList built once at module load from exactly the six ranges requirement 7 names (127/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16 as ipv4 subnets; ::1 as an ipv6 address). BlockList.check() evaluates the address's value, not its string, so IPv4-mapped IPv6 in either spelling is checked against the IPv4 rules. This closes the class of bug (string-form matching against a normalized form the string never takes), not just the one instance.
Re-ran the round-1 probes, unchanged:
  1. normalizeAndValidateUrl() now REJECTS all four bracketed forms — http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/, http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/, http://[::ffff:c0a8:10a]/ (=192.168.1.10), http://[::ffff:a00:1]/ (=10.0.0.1) — each with the field-level private-address message. Round 1 accepted every one.
  2. Reachability repro: HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1 only; all four URLs are now rejected by the validator pre-flight. Round 1 reached the server and got 200.
  3. Falsification (no over-blocking): ::ffff:8.8.8.8, ::ffff:808:808, 2001:4860:4860::8888, 8.8.8.8, 172.15.255.255, 172.32.0.0, 192.167.255.255, ::2 all still allowed. Public control http://example.com/ still accepted. Every alternate IPv4 spelling (hex/decimal/short/octal) still rejected. localhost still rejected via /etc/hosts.
Tests: the new urlValidation.test.js cases go through new URL() with bracketed literals in both dotted and hex spellings — the real path — which is what round 1 asked for. The hex-spelling case is asserted directly too, so the test survives even if URL's own serializer changes. 117/117 pass, lint exit 0, tests stayed off disk, tree clean.

CODE QUALITY (fix only)
Simpler than what it replaced: 41 lines vs 55, no manual octet parsing, no regex. The module comment explains the actual bug and why BlockList is the fix rather than a patched regex. This is fine.

NON-BLOCKING ITEMS CARRIED FROM ROUND 1 — unchanged, still open, none required for ship
  2. [LOW] Deleted ciphertext persists in freed SQLite pages until VACUUM; PRAGMA secure_delete=ON in openDatabase() is a one-liner. Ciphertext only, within the sprint's threat model.
  3. [LOW] 0.0.0.0, [::], [fe80::]/10, [fc00::]/7 still accepted — re-confirmed this round. Outside requirement 7's explicit list, so not a gate item. Now that the check is BlockList-based these are four more addSubnet lines. Master Controller should decide whether Sprint 3's request-time check widens the list; QA1 will be looking for the request-time check there regardless (the DNS fail-open decision recorded in round 1 depends on it).
  4. [LOW] values.rawPassword reaches EJS locals on validation-error re-render; not rendered (verified round 1), but strip it before render.
  5. [INFO] parsed.origin normalization silently drops userinfo from a pasted URL.

HANDOFF NOTE FOR LIVEQA
Round-1 notes carry the full verification detail for all eleven requirements; this round re-verified only the SSRF fix. Everything LiveQA needs to test is described in the sprint file's two LiveQA criteria: the Back-button/bfcache check on the project list (log in, create a project with a password, log out, Back — the page must reload to login, not re-render from cache), and the full create / edit-blank-keeps / edit-new-password / clear / delete walkthrough with the delete confirmation step actually blocking a one-click delete. If you try a private-address URL in the form, expect the message "This URL points to a private, loopback, or link-local address, which this tool cannot fetch." on the field, not a generic error.
